title: Nice names and exact continuum values in Cohen extensions
summary: Replace real names by antichain codes and count them to determine the continuum in suitable Cohen extensions.
abstract: Adding many Cohen reals gives a lower bound for the continuum, but an exact value also requires an upper bound on every real in the extension. Under the countable chain condition, each real can be named using a countable antichain for each natural number. These nice names form a set whose ground-model size is controlled by a countable cardinal power. An explicit name for their evaluation map turns this count into a bound inside the extension. Combining that bound with the Cohen-column injection determines the continuum when the ground cardinal satisfies the stated power identity. In particular, a given externally countable transitive model of ZFC and CH has a cardinal-preserving Cohen extension whose continuum is exactly its second uncountable cardinal.
